examples.before:
.troupe/troupe.yml:
a: file:sub/a.yaml
up: file:sub/upper.YML  # upper-case suffix

.troupe/sub/a.yaml:
inner: file:b.txt

(both .troupe/b.txt and .troupe/sub/b.txt exist)

results.1: all three arms: exit 0, prints `text from .troupe/sub/b.txt`, so the path is resolved next to sub/a.yaml, the file that includes it
results.2: all three arms: exit 0, prints `text from .troupe/sub/b.txt`

examples.before:
up: file:sub/upper.YML  # upper-case suffix

.troupe/sub/upper.YML:
k: v

results.1: all three arms: exit 0, prints `k: v` (`config show` lists it as a block of text `up: |`, so the upper-case .YML file is read as text, not YAML)
results.2: all three arms: exit 0, prints `k: v`, also shown as text `up: |`

results.1: two arms: exit 3, refused as an include cycle (e.g. `written value cannot be read back: ... include cycle: /theatre/.troupe/loop.yaml -> /theatre/.troupe/sub/../loop.yaml`); one arm: exit 4, `troupe: .troupe/loop.yaml: include cycle (from .troupe/loop.yaml)`. In all three, no file changed and `config get a.inner` still works afterwards
results.2: all three arms: exit 3, refused as an include cycle (e.g. `troupe: loop: include cycle at loop.again: /theatre/.troupe/loop.yaml -> /theatre/.troupe/loop.yaml; no file changed`). No file changed and `config get a.inner` still works afterwards

context.in_practice: On every read, both routes gave the same results. On both routes, every arm caught the cycle even though it was hidden behind `sub/../`, and every arm refused it without touching the config. Route 1 says cycles exit 4, but only one of its arms did that. Its other two arms, and every arm of route 2, exited 3, which is the code for a refused write.
context.stakes: Config values can pull in other files (`file:...`). If a relative path resolves against the wrong directory, if an upper-case `.YML` file is read the wrong way, or if a self-including file is accepted, the user gets the wrong value or a config that will no longer load. In these runs both routes behaved the same on every read. They differed only in the exit code when a cycle was refused, and even there route 1's arms did not all agree.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 commits to fixed rules (case-sensitive suffix, paths relative to the including file, exit 4 on cycles) that one arm did not follow for exit codes. Route 2 never stated a rule but behaved the same here, with exit 3 on every arm.

plan_why: Shows three include behaviours: a nested include inside .troupe/sub/a.yaml is resolved relative to that file (two b.txt files with different text), a target ending in upper-case .YML is read as text or as YAML, and adding an include that loops back through sub/../ is either rejected with exit 4 or not, plus what happens to the config afterwards.
routes: YAML include by .yml/.yaml suffix (case-sensitive), else text; paths relative to the including file; cycles and missing or non-UTF-8 targets exit 4
